title: Eight Muslim Nations Condemn Israel's Rejection of Gaza Peace Road Map
excerpt: Foreign ministers of UAE, Qatar, Jordan and five other nations say Israel bears full responsibility for obstructing Trump's peace plan endorsed by the UN Security Council.
body:
• Eight Arab and Muslim-majority nations condemned Israel's rejection of the Road Map for implementing Trump's Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, endorsed by UN Security Council Resolution 2803.
  • The foreign ministers of UAE, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt said Israel now bears responsibility for obstructing peace efforts.
  • Palestinian factions have accepted the Road Map, which includes weapons decommissioning, Israeli withdrawal, and deployment of an International Stabilization Force.
  • The ministers called for sustained US engagement to enforce Israel's compliance and rejected any denial of Palestinian statehood.

The foreign ministers of eight Arab and Muslim-majority nations issued a sharp joint statement on August 16 condemning Israel's declared rejection of the Road Map for completing Trump's Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. The statement marks a significant escalation in diplomatic pressure on Israel from some of its closest regional interlocutors.

The ministers—representing the UAE, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt—said Israel's rejection of both the Road Map and Palestinian statehood "amount to a direct repudiation of the Comprehensive Plan" and "fundamentally undermine the collective efforts undertaken to achieve a just and lasting peace."

What the Road Map Entails

The Road Map, which Palestinian factions have accepted, emerged from extensive negotiations involving mediators Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, the United States, the High Representative of Gaza, and the Board of Peace. It lays out a sequence of steps: decommissioning of weapons concurrent with Israeli forces' withdrawal, deployment of an International Stabilization Force, transfer of administrative authority to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, and reconstruction of the territory.

The plan is rooted in UN Security Council Resolution 2803, which endorsed Trump's broader Comprehensive Plan. Israel's refusal to proceed with the Road Map, the ministers said, "constitutes an explicit refusal to proceed with the implementation of the Comprehensive Plan" and threatens to derail Trump's efforts to end the war.

Responsibility Shifts to Israel

In pointed language, the joint statement declared that Israel "now bears responsibility for obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza." The ministers stressed that Israel carries "direct and full responsibility for any consequences resulting from its continued rejection, obstruction, delay or non-compliance, including any resulting deterioration of the situation on the ground."

"Such rejection confirms that Israel now bears responsibility for obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza and the rest of the Occupied Palestinian Territory."

— Joint Statement, Foreign Ministers of UAE, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Türkiye, KSA, and Egypt

The statement underscored the need for "sustained and active US engagement to ensure and enforce Israel's full compliance" with the plan. It also called on the Board of Peace to take "immediate and concrete measures" to prevent any party from obstructing implementation.

Escalating Context

The joint statement builds on months of coordinated diplomatic pressure from these eight nations. On August 6, the same group of foreign ministers condemned ongoing Israeli violations in Gaza, including strikes on healthcare facilities and civilian infrastructure. Israel has continued strikes since agreeing to a US-mediated ceasefire last October, killing 1,200 Palestinians in nine months, according to Palestinian health officials. Israeli officials countered that Hamas continues to rearm and rebuild tunnels.

In July, the ministers also condemned Israeli escalation at Al-Aqsa Mosque, including mass settler incursions led by extremist Israeli ministers under the protection of Israeli forces.

Two-State Solution Reaffirmed

The ministers categorically rejected "any attempt to deny or foreclose Palestinian statehood including through unilateral actions," reaffirming that lasting peace requires "an independent and sovereign Palestinian State based on the 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital." They warned that Israel's rejection of Palestinian statehood "directly undermines the prospects for peace, security and stability throughout the region."

Gulf Stability and Diaspora Impact

India maintains close ties with several signatory nations, particularly the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, which collectively host millions of Indian workers. The escalation in Gaza and the diplomatic fallout continue to affect energy markets and regional stability in the Gulf, where an estimated 8.5 million Indians live and work. Rising tensions could impact remittance flows and oil prices that directly affect the Indian economy.
